No assertion maps; the only shared lines are the Machine stand-ins and CLI dispatch.

Its assertions (status lists the required chain, a hand edit of a required role's file is drift of the requiring role, update moves required roles to the new rev, update of a required-only role is refused) have no counterpart in global_status_and_update_follow_the_source_and_leave_the_project_alone, whose role requires nothing and is installed --global; folding them in would change its library and its global-vs-project setup

its assertions (exit 2, empty stdout, the flag named on stderr) are on agent-context --no-such-flag, which the global test never runs; global.rs's fixture is another file's setup
it checks the library topic's text, which the errors topic test never reads; separate topics, no shared run to save
it checks the errors topic's rules and problem keys, which no other test reads; the library and sources topics are other runs

kept_files.reason: Already deep: one entry point, load(root, only) -> Library | every Problem, hides reading, TOML/YAML parsing, line finding, requires closure and cycle check, external-skill fetch, tool pinning and the secret scan; callers use only load, the parsed types, valid_name, split_front_matter, Install::pinned and the limits. Its 14 commits in 90 days are features (requires, [[skill]], script install, brew stable, [service]) each adding its check to the one home of library validation, which is where they belong. Tests go through the binary; the three unit tests cover pure helpers only. Splitting the schema types from the Checker would move lines without hiding anything.

Already deep: callers use sync, install, drift, locate, named_position, Record::load/save, known_projects, Place and the TARGETS table; behind them it hides planning every role's files (requires closure, two-rev conflicts), rendering a role into installed skills (core skill, renamed SKILL.md front matter, symlink refusal), the foreign-file refusal, manifest diffing, write-if-changed with the exec bit, empty-dir cleanup, the .gitignore block and the projects file. Its 16 commits in 90 days are features (global installs, targets, requires, external skills, entry files, doctor --project) each adding to this one home of what an install writes. Tests go through the binary; the one unit test covers the pure parse_projects. Splitting the role renderer or .gitignore block into modules would move lines without narrowing any interface.

Already deep: its one interface is the doctor command (Args::run); behind it it hides resolving one role or every recorded and required role of a project at its rev, running each program's check here or on a host over ssh, reading mytokens by name only, splitting needs into mytokens entries and services.toml-mapped services, running each service's check, naming what its command asks for, probing it without a person and keeping the outcome, and turning every gap into one refusal with its fix. The work itself lives in deeper modules it composes (needs, machine, host, probe, service_map); nothing else calls into doctor.rs, and its tests go through the binary (no unit tests reach past it). Its 12 commits in 90 days are features (tool show split, --host, --project, script and brew-stable tools, mapped services, --probe), each adding its check to the one home of what doctor reports. Moving services() into probe or service_map would only move lines and put doctor's human and JSON answer into a lower module; Run is the small per-mode description the two entry points share.
